name: Motorcycle
description: A road-registered motor vehicle with handlebars and a straddle seat on no more than three wheels; an electric one whose motor produces more than 5 horsepower (3,750 W) is a full motorcycle rather than a motor-driven cycle. Defined by Hawaii Revised Statutes §286-2 and §291C-1, with "motor vehicle" expressly covering vehicles propelled by electric power.

restrictions.rule: Handlebars and a seat the rider straddles, on no more than three wheels, or a federally certified three-wheeled autocycle; a moped is excluded
Its motor produces more than 5 horsepower (3,750 W); one at or below that is a motor-driven cycle, under the same license, helmet and insurance rules
Riders need a motorcycle license (category 2); an instruction permit requires a state-approved basic motorcycle rider course, and its holder can't ride after dark or carry passengers
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a safety helmet fastened with a chin strap, unless it's an electric three-wheeler with a roll cage or enclosed cab and seat belts that they wear
Riders and passengers must wear safety glasses, goggles or a face shield unless it has a windscreen
Registered with the county director of finance and must pass a safety inspection every year once it is two years past its first sale
Must carry liability insurance of at least $20,000 per person, $40,000 per accident and $10,000 property damage
Not allowed in bike lanes or on bike paths; one whose electric motor can exceed 28 mph is also an electric motorcycle, barred from any path or roadway designated for bicycles
